bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Delayed/patchy summer season impacting fans/coolers; War-geopolitical input cost inflation; Market share loss in Fans due to BLDC technology gap; Demand uncertainty limiting price pass-through.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; Transparent about Consumer Products struggles; Confident in Lighting trajectory; Emphasis on 'cultural change' and sustainable profitability over volume push.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management explicitly stated they will reinvest Lighting margin gains to accelerate growth rather than bottom-line expansion; Fan segment weakness specifically tied to lack of competitive BLDC offerings vs. traditional induction strength; Inventory correction in coolers still ongoing but deemed non-material for full year.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Lighting Solutions: 16% Q4 revenue growth, 8.7% Q4 EBIT margin, 8.5% annual EBIT margin. Consumer Products: Kitchen appliances +30% growth; Fans and Coolers negative due to delayed summer and high channel inventory; Irons/Water Heaters modest growth. Wires: New entry with strong market response.

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Intent to grow ahead of market (mid-single digit industry avg). Margin: Lighting EBIT likely stable as gains reinvested for growth; Consumer targetting industry avg 6-9% EBIT over medium term. Order Inflow: Strong in Wires/Switchgears. Capex: Substantial reduction in FY27/FY28 (<50% of past levels), focused on mould replacement and innovation.

outlook.body: Wires category as new growth driver; Bridging BLDC fan technology gap to recover market share; Premiumization in Lighting; Expansion in Professional Lighting.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Bajaj Electricals delivered a modest Q4FY26 with Lighting Solutions hitting record margins (8.5% annual) while Consumer Products faced losses due to delayed summer and intentional channel de-stocking. The strategic pivot from volume-push to demand-led sell-through is progressing, with inventory normalization expected to drive a rebound in FY27, though fan market share erosion due to BLDC gaps remains a critical near-term headwind.

risks.note: The AR flags high macroeconomic uncertainty, shifting trade policies and continuing fiscal challenges; geopolitical tensions in the Middle East add pressure, with disruptions in key shipping routes potentially raising freight costs and lead times, and volatility in crude oil and base metal prices (copper, aluminium) potentially raising input costs — directly relevant given Bajaj Electricals' exposure to copper/aluminium as commodity inputs.
risks.risk: Geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty (Middle East conflict, shifting trade policies)

risks.note: The rupee hit an all-time low of approximately ₹95/USD during the year, driven by Middle East conflict volatility and FPI outflows; a weakening rupee accelerates domestic inflation by raising import costs (especially crude oil) and widens the trade deficit, which the Company is exposed to given import dependence in its supply chain.
Tariff-related trade disruptions and volatility in capital flows may intermittently affect exports and investor sentiment, per the MD&A macro outlook.

Supply-chain disruptions due to the West Asia conflict could tighten the availability of key inputs for downstream sectors, including plastics and aluminium — materials relevant to the Company's manufacturing base.
risks.risk: Supply-chain disruption from the West Asia conflict

risks.note: Import dependence exposes companies (including Bajaj Electricals) to currency fluctuations and supply disruptions from geopolitical conflicts, which may elevate input costs; separately, regulatory bodies such as the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) are strictly enforcing Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) norms, leading to increased product recalls and legal notices for non-compliant goods on e-commerce platforms.
risks.risk: Import dependence and tightening regulatory/quality enforcement

risks.note: Competition remains vigorous, intensified by established global and domestic players and low barriers to entry; aggressive pricing, frequent discounts and new product launches can weigh on margins over time.

The Consolidated Financial Analysis shows revenue, EBITDA, EBIT and PAT margins all declining year-on-year in FY26, with the Company moving from profit to loss at the PBT/PAT/Return-on-Net-Worth level — reflecting an operating-deleverage risk if demand softness persists.

The external Internal Auditor identified certain non-significant automated controls not configured during the year; these were mitigated by compensating manual controls, but represent a residual internal-control risk to monitor.
risks.risk: Internal control gaps in automated systems
